page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at the top left, printed page number at the top right. Under the text: a catchword at the right and a gathering signature at the left. A small-capital heading stands in the middle of the page, followed by paragraphs and an indented verse passage.

main_text.p: Quid sperandum sit de clementia Dei & malorum mitigatione, postrema edi-cti istius pars, uerf.9.oftendit.
main_text.head: DE PERSONIS EARUM-que circumstantijs.
main_text.p: Si ὑπόθεσιν [?] uersus 7.ad thesin reducas, occurret haec doctrina: Decreta magistratus exercitijs poenitentiae seruire debent.

Vt hoc loco dicitur, Regem Assyriorum eiusq; συμπαραστάτας [?], regni Proceres, edictum de resipiscentiae exercitijs praescri-psisse subditis, ut ad laudabile Regis ad Deum conuersi exemplum, salutaris eiusdem per edictum exhortatio accederet.

p.i: Tu ciuem patremq; geras, tu consule cunctis: In commune iubes si quid censesq; tenendum, Primus iussa subi. tunc obseruantior æqui Fit populus, nec ferre uetat, cum uiderit ipsum Auctorem parere sibi. componitur orbis Regis ad exemplum: nec sic inflectere sensus Humanos edicta ualent, quàm uita regentis. Mobile mutatur semper cum Principe uulgus.

main_text.p: Nonnihil simile est exemplum Nebucadnezaris magni, qui à Deo grauiter correptus, ubi ad sanitatem mentis reuoca-

page.notes: Greek words in the text ("ὑπόθεσιν", "συμπαραστάτας") are my best reading of the scan and are marked [?]. The "u" in the heading word EARUM is printed as V and was changed to a vowel u. The verse passage is set in italic; I kept it as one stanza. The catchword "tus" and the signature are at the foot. No marginal notes are printed on this page.
